definition: A retrieval approach that combines keyword-based (lexical) search with embedding-based (semantic) search to leverage the strengths of both.
details: Hybrid search helps address cases where pure semantic search misses exact term matches (like product codes or rare proper nouns) that keyword search handles well, while still benefiting from semantic search's ability to match meaning.
story: Think of a grammar teacher who never memorized a rule but can still tell you when a sentence sounds wrong. The machine learns language the way you did — by hearing so much of it that the patterns sink in. It figures out meaning by noticing which words like to travel together. The machine learns to read between the lines by reading an impossible number of lines. That pattern-earned fluency is Hybrid Search.
